source: synthetic. The last-resort permission wait upstream's
        `legacy_no_prompt_blocker` is written for, transcribed from that rule's
        own literal ("waiting for permission") rather than captured: it is the
        shape Claude leaves on screen when a tool is held pending approval and
        the prompt itself has not been drawn.
why: this is the fixture the `legacy_no_prompt_blocker` overlay is kept for.
     Upstream declares the rule blocked with no `visible_blocker`, so the pane
     lands on the blocked lane with no attention flag and every surface that
     keys an alert on `Tracker.VisibleBlocker` stays quiet — which before the
     manifest cutover it did not. The overlay in manifests/sidecar/claude.toml
     replaces the rule by id, verbatim plus `visible_blocker = true`, so the
     verdict and the rule id are unchanged and only the nag comes back.
